DuplicateRelationship.description:
Sub-classification used when independence has been rejected.

Distinguishes a likely-duplicate report pair from one where the
pair is linked by something other than being the same individual
case (e.g. same reporter, same study, two patients on the same
unusual regimen). The decision logic chooses between these based
on the weighted inconsistency score ``w_tot``.

Mirrors the user-facing label vocabulary (``Duplicates`` /
``Otherwise_related``).

``ABSTAIN`` is reserved for future abstain paths and currently
unused — the decision logic only ever assigns ``DUPLICATES`` or
``OTHERWISE_RELATED``. The value is kept so ``final_label`` can map
it defensively if a future code path produces one.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Decision logic
DuplicateRelationship.title: DuplicateRelationship

IndependenceAssessment.description:
Internal independence assessment produced by the decision logic.

Captures whether the rarity-based matching evidence is strong
enough to reject the null hypothesis that the two reports are
independent draws from the comparison population. A
``NON_INDEPENDENT`` verdict means the matched features are too
unlikely to have arisen by chance under that null; the duplicate
vs otherwise-related distinction is then made by the
``DuplicateRelationship`` sub-label using inconsistency signals.

The user-facing label is derived from this enum (plus
``DuplicateRelationship``) by ``ClassificationResult.final_label``;
downstream consumers should depend on the final label rather than
on this raw enum.

``ABSTAIN`` is reserved for future abstain paths and currently
unused — the decision logic only ever assigns ``NON_INDEPENDENT`` or
``INDEPENDENT``. The value is kept so ``final_label`` can map it
defensively if a future code path produces one.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Decision logic
IndependenceAssessment.title: IndependenceAssessment

IndependenceReason.description:
Audit trail for which branch in the decision logic fired.

Attached to :class:`ClassificationResult` so downstream review can
tell *why* a pair landed on its independence assessment. The
``RARITY_*`` values correspond to the four L_match zones of the
rarity-based branch; ``SHARED_SOURCE`` is set by the shared-source
override path (when a reliable shared source identifier has been
derived from the narratives). ``ABSTAIN`` is reserved for future
abstain paths and currently unused.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Decision logic
IndependenceReason.title: IndependenceReason

description:
Full duplicate-adjudication output for a report pair.

Two layered internal labels are produced by the decision logic:

* ``independence_assessment`` — whether the rarity-based matching
  evidence is strong enough to reject the null hypothesis that the
  two reports are independent draws from the comparison population.
* ``duplicate_relationship`` — when independence has been rejected,
  a sub-label that uses inconsistency signals to distinguish a
  likely-duplicate case from one that is linked by something other
  than being the same individual case (e.g. same reporter, same
  study).

Use ``final_label`` for the user-facing label
(``Duplicates`` / ``Otherwise_related`` / ``Unrelated``); downstream
consumers should depend on this rather than on the raw internal
fields.
